title: U.S. House · New York's 19th Congressional District
area: Central New York/Catskills/Mid-Hudson region, covering all or part of Sullivan, Delaware, Otsego, Schoharie, Broome, Tioga, Chenango, Cortland, Chemung, Tompkins, and Columbia counties.

context.text: This is a rematch of the 2024 general election, when incumbent Josh Riley defeated Peter Oberacker's predecessor, then-Rep. Marcus Molinaro, 51.1% to 48.8% (Molinaro had defeated Riley 50.8%-49.2% in 2022 under different lines). Oberacker won the June 23, 2026 Republican primary over Alexander Portelli, 77.4% to 22.1%; Riley's Democratic primary was canceled.

Kamala Harris carried the district 50.4% to 48.7% in 2024. As of September 22, 2026, all four major forecasters (Cook Political Report, Decision Desk, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball) rated the general election "Likely Democratic." As of June 30, 2026, Riley had raised $4.83 million to Oberacker's $1.24 million.

summary.text: Josh Riley is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for New York's 19th Congressional District. An Endicott native and Harvard-trained lawyer, he worked as a Labor Department analyst, Senate Judiciary Committee counsel and law firm partner before narrowly losing the seat in 2022 and winning it in 2024. He sits on the Agriculture and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

background.text: Born in Endicott, New York, in 1981 and a 1999 graduate of Union-Endicott High School; his official biography says his family worked in local factories including Endicott-Johnson and IBM.
Earned a bachelor's degree in government and economics from the College of William & Mary in 2003 and a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 2007.
Early in his career he was an aide to Rep. Maurice Hinchey (D-NY) and a policy analyst at the U.S. Department of Labor.

After law school he worked as an associate at Boies Schiller Flexner and clerked for Judge Kim McLane Wardlaw of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit; his official biography says he represented children from low-income families in a landmark civil rights case on access to health care.

Served as general counsel to Sen. Al Franken (D-MN) on the Senate Judiciary Committee (2011-2014, per Wikipedia), where his official biography says he worked on addiction treatment programs and corporate accountability.
Later returned to Boies Schiller Flexner as a partner until 2021, then was a partner at Jenner & Block.
Lost the 2022 general election for NY-19 to Rep. Marc Molinaro (R/Conservative), 50.8%-49.2%, then defeated Molinaro 51.1%-48.8% in 2024; sworn in January 3, 2025.
In the House he serves on the Agriculture Committee and the Science, Space, and Technology Committee, and his official biography lists campaign finance reform among his priorities.
Lives in Ithaca with his wife, Monica, and their two sons, according to his official biography.

priorities.text: Campaign material says he worked on bipartisan legislation to protect survivors of domestic violence and combat the opioid epidemic, and on legislation to restore the Voting Rights Act and reduce the influence of money in politics.
priorities.quote: helped pass bipartisan legislation to protect survivors of domestic violence and combat the opioid epidemic. He worked on legislation to restore the Voting Rights Act, and he led efforts to overturn Citizens United and end the influence of dark money in politics.

priorities.text: Has criticized Oberacker's state legislative record on utility rates, health insurance, and taxes, saying Oberacker has "helped the utility monopolies raise rates while cashing their corporate PAC checks" and raised taxes on working people 14 times.

record.text: Serves on the House Agriculture Committee (Livestock, Dairy, and Poultry subcommittee) and the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee (Energy subcommittee) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

summary.text: Peter Oberacker is a Republican and Conservative New York State Senator for District 51, first elected in 2020, and the Republican nominee for NY-19. A SUNY Delhi graduate who grew up in a family meat market, he worked as a food scientist and founded FormTech Solutions before serving as a town supervisor and Otsego County legislator. He won the June 23, 2026 Republican primary and is challenging incumbent Josh Riley.

background.text: Born in Merrick, New York, in 1963 and raised in Schenevus, where he worked in his family's meat market from childhood, according to Wikipedia and a campaign-website biography reproduced by Ballotpedia.
Graduated from Schenevus High School and from SUNY Delhi (1983, per Wikipedia).
Worked with his father at Spicey Pete's Meat Market and became a research chef and food scientist; the state Senate site says he specialized in beef, pork and poultry ingredient formulations.
Founded FormTech Solutions, a food-innovation company; his campaign website says he moved its headquarters to his hometown in 2017.
Served two terms on the Maryland, New York town board and two terms as town supervisor, then as an Otsego County legislator.
Elected to the State Senate in November 2020 with 55.4% of the vote, succeeding James Seward, and took office January 1, 2021; he was re-elected in 2024.

In the Senate he is ranking member of the Alcoholism and Substance Use Disorders and Transportation committees and a member of Agriculture, Finance, Higher Education and Labor; his stated focus is rural emergency services, agriculture, broadband and infrastructure.
Has volunteered with the C.H. Graham Hose Company for nearly 40 years, is a SUNY Delhi Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, and is a member of the Masonic Lodge; he lives in Schenevus.

priorities.text: Campaign material emphasizes his state legislative record of "keeping taxes low" and never having created a budget that raised taxes, along with an emphasis on being visible and present in the district.
priorities.quote: he has focused on delivering results, keeping taxes low, and standing up for the people he represents. He has never created a budget that raised taxes.

positions.summary: Says he has never sponsored a state budget that raised taxes and campaigns on keeping taxes low.

record.text: In the 119th New York State Senate session (2025-2026), serves as Ranking Member of the Senate Alcoholism and Substance Abuse Committee and the Senate Transportation Committee, and sits on the Agriculture, Finance, Higher Education, and Labor Committees.
Was re-elected to New York State Senate District 51 on November 5, 2024, defeating Michele Frazier.

researchNotes: Neither Riley nor Oberacker had completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; priorities and positions draw on campaign-website material republished by Ballotpedia. Oberacker's list of sponsored state-senate bills could not be retrieved (Ballotpedia's bill table and nysenate.gov both required JavaScript/blocked automated access), so his record here is limited to committee assignments and election history. Oberacker's and Riley's biographies draw on official pages plus Wikipedia for birth years and career dates.
